EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development of the past 24 hours is the last-minute cancellation of a major planned US military strike against Iran by President Trump, who attributed it to an "agreement in principle" for the full opening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat. This claim was immediately and vehemently denied by Iran, which maintains the Strait remains closed and that no such deal was reached, creating significant ambiguity and tension.

IRAN
Iranian acting Defense Minister Brigadier General Seyyed Majid Ibn Al-Reza stated that Iran's armed forces will neither be taken by surprise nor sit idly by in the face of threats, considering every threat to be real and using them to raise preparedness and deterrence. The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) affirmed that attempts to disarm Hamas are futile and vowed severe retaliation for the assassination of Ismail Haniyeh. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reported that negotiations with Oman concerning a "new mechanism" for the Strait of Hormuz are in their final stages, but clarified that this does not signify the Strait's reopening. Araghchi also warned Turkey and Pakistan that any US or Israeli aggression, or regional participation, would face a "decisive" and "powerful" response. President Pezeshkian endorsed a memorandum, the result of collective wisdom from SNSC members, as the cornerstone of future foreign relations, enhancing regional security. Internally, one soldier, Abulfazl Goodarzi, was martyred in a drone and RPG attack by the PJAK group on a military base in Marivan at 03:00 local time today. Reports of internet slowdowns and outages were noted in cities including Abadan, Tabriz, Damavand, and Isfahan. Economically, the government reduced the second fuel quota (at 3,000 Tomans) from 70 to 50 liters per month starting August 6, and the US dollar price neared 196,000 Tomans. The Trump administration also prohibited the import of Chinese robots for national security reasons.

ISRAEL
The IDF announced the elimination of three terror operatives in Gaza who were advancing attacks: Alaa Imad Khamis Tarams of the Army of Islam and Hassan Ibrahim Shehadeh Qahman of Palestinian Islamic Jihad in Gaza City yesterday, and Ahmad Khudar, a Hamas Jabalia Battalion commander, in North Gaza last week. Additionally, Salem Jamal Abd al-Rahman Abu Labad, a Hamas Nukhba cell head who infiltrated Kibbutz Nir Oz on October 7, and Muhammad Abd al-Nasser Muhammad Khatib, a Hamas Maghazi Battalion commander, were killed in strikes in South and Central Gaza respectively over the weekend. Combat Team 401 concluded an 8-month mission in South Lebanon, during which it confiscated over 600 weapons and eliminated more than 60 Hezbollah terrorists. On the home front, a 65-year-old man was moderately injured with penetrating wounds in Rahat. A 35-year-old man was killed, and 9 others were injured in a traffic accident on Road 98 near Afik in the southern Golan Heights. Fires prompted the evacuation of the first line of houses in Kfar Salon, near Beit Shemesh. Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu stated in a closed discussion that a "full conscription law" would be passed after the next elections, asserting that Haredim who do not study Torah would be conscripted or jailed, a stance criticized by MK Hili Trooper and United Torah Judaism's Goldknopf, who argued that the temporary arrest law "did not succeed." Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich advocated for re-settling Gaza with Jews after full control and opposed multi-national forces. Israel expressed frustration over Trump's unpredictable decision-making regarding Iran. American Airlines extended the cancellation of its flights to Ben Gurion Airport until March 27, 2027.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Despite a ceasefire roadmap, Palestinian medical sources reported 6-8 Palestinians, including 2 children, were killed in Israeli airstrikes across the Gaza Strip. A drone strike in Jabalia refugee camp in North Gaza resulted in one fatality and several injuries. The body of an unborn child was recovered from the womb of its mother after an Israeli attack destroyed a residential building in Gaza City. The IDF justified its continued targeted killings, including those of Hamas, PIJ, and Army of Islam operatives, by stating they were advancing terror plots against Israeli forces and citizens. Israel maintains it will not cease attacks until Hamas is disarmed. A Hamas official reiterated that the newly announced agreement does not involve surrendering weapons but outlines a conditional, Palestinian-led process contingent on Tel Aviv's adherence to its obligations. In the West Bank, extremist Israeli settlers carried out attacks overnight and on Sunday morning, injuring several Palestinians and damaging homes, vehicles, and infrastructure. Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett vowed to declare Qatar an "enemy" if re-elected, alleging Qatar funded Hamas's October 7 infiltration.

LEBANON
Five Lebanese soldiers were lightly injured today when their vehicle struck an explosive device in the town of Kafra, South Lebanon. The Lebanese Armed Forces initially attributed the blast to an Israeli strike but later revised the cause to a "suspicious object." The IDF denied any involvement, stating its forces were never present in Kafra, which is outside its south Lebanon buffer zone, and assessed the device belonged to Hezbollah. The IDF also announced that Combat Team 401 completed its 8-month mission in South Lebanon, during which it seized over 600 weapons and eliminated more than 60 Hezbollah terrorists. Israeli forces were reported to have set fire to vast areas of land in al-Tayyiba village and conducted demolition operations in Taybeh, both in South Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Attacks continued against Kurdish-Iranian opposition forces in North Iraq. Drone strikes were reported in Sulaymaniyah and Erbil, hitting "separatist Kurdish terrorists" headquarters. Explosions occurred at the Al-Taji military base north of Baghdad, with Iraq's Security Media Cell attributing them to high temperatures in an ammunition depot. US military aircraft (C-130J) were tracked landing in western Iraq after departing from Aqaba, Jordan. The Iraqi government denied reports of US aircraft landing at Ain al-Asad Air Base. Iraqi National Security Advisor Qassem Al-Araji agreed to open a NATO office in Baghdad. In a separate incident, a traffic accident involving a bus carrying Iranian pilgrims in Wasit province resulted in the martyrdom of several Iranian visitors and an Iraqi colonel and soldier. The Syrian-Jordanian border region was active, with Jordan announcing a new emergency message system and reports of air raid sirens sounding in Jordan. Ahmed al-Shara reportedly ordered the deployment of forces to Syria's borders with Lebanon and Iraq. The Golani government, in agreement with the Bahraini Embassy in Damascus, is reported to have prevented Shia pilgrims from Bahrain from entering Syria for religious visits.

GULF STATES
Diplomatic efforts focused on de-escalation: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) held talks with US President Trump, expressing concern over potential extensive US attacks on Iran and urging de-escalation, as reported by CNN and Axios. Separately, the foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Qatar discussed efforts to unify positions to reduce regional tensions. However, some Gulf states, notably the UAE, were reported by the Wall Street Journal and N12 to be pushing Trump for more decisive action against Iran, including taking control of the Strait of Hormuz and considering ground operations, believing Iran will not compromise without escalation. Oman is in "final stages" of negotiations with Iran regarding a "new mechanism" for the Strait of Hormuz, with reports suggesting Oman is seeking formal confirmation from the IRGC for any agreement. Kuwaiti government-aligned social media accounts reposted archival videos expressing gratitude for US protection, coinciding with Iranian threats. A US C-17 transport aircraft was observed heading towards Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, potentially carrying radar replacements. OPEC+ agreed to increase oil production by 188,000 barrels per day for September. CENTCOM claimed to have diverted 35 ships and disabled two since Iran's port blockade was reimposed.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1. US President Trump unilaterally canceled a planned major military strike on Iran, citing an "agreement in principle" for the "immediate, complete, and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz" and an end to Iran's nuclear threat.
2. Iran's Foreign Ministry and state media (Fars News Agency) immediately and strongly denied any agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, stating it remains closed and that Trump's claims are "false news."
3. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi confirmed ongoing, nearing-completion negotiations with Oman for a "new mechanism" for the Strait of Hormuz but clarified that this does not mean the Strait is being reopened.
4. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) contacted President Trump to express concern over potential large-scale US attacks on Iran and advocated for de-escalation. In contrast, the UAE reportedly urged Trump to take more decisive military action against Iran.
5. Five Lebanese soldiers were injured in Kafra, South Lebanon, by an explosion. While the Lebanese army initially blamed an Israeli strike, they later revised the cause to a "suspicious object," and the IDF denied involvement, asserting the device was planted by Hezbollah.
6. The IDF announced the completion of Combat Team 401's 8-month mission in South Lebanon, having confiscated over 600 weapons and eliminated more than 60 Hezbollah terrorists.
7. The IDF continued targeted killings in Gaza, eliminating at least five terror operatives from Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, and the Army of Islam, including a Hamas Nukhba cell head who infiltrated Kibbutz Nir Oz on October 7. These actions drew criticism from the US for undermining ceasefire efforts.
8. One Iranian soldier, Abulfazl Goodarzi, was killed in a drone and RPG attack by the PJAK group on a military base in Marivan, Kurdistan province, Iran, early today.
9. An LNG tanker, GasLog Shanghai, was reportedly struck by a projectile in its engine room and lost power while attempting to exit the Strait of Hormuz off the Omani coast.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high, despite Trump's announced cancellation of strikes. The fundamental disagreement between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran denying any agreement to reopen it, creates a significant flashpoint. Iran's acting Defense Minister and IRGC statements indicate an unwavering posture of defense and readiness for retaliation against any aggression from the US, Israel, or regional partners, explicitly extending to regional states that cooperate with such actions. The alleged projectile strike on the LNG tanker GasLog Shanghai in the Strait of Hormuz, if confirmed, represents a critical and direct escalation of maritime conflict. Active flashpoints include Gaza, where Israeli targeted killings continue despite ceasefire efforts and US criticism, and South Lebanon, following the Kafra incident and the conclusion of an IDF operation against Hezbollah. North Iraq also remains a conflict zone with attacks on Kurdish-Iranian opposition forces. Military postures indicate high readiness: the US maintains a significant presence of aerial refueling aircraft at Ben Gurion in Israel (up to 40 planes) and the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier in the Gulf of Oman, while Iran signals increased preparedness. Israel's leadership expressed frustration with US unpredictability but maintains high alert. Red lines for Iran include attacks on its infrastructure and national sovereignty, with threats of robust responses, while the US aims for the complete opening of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** posture is mixed: President Trump announced the cancellation of planned strikes, citing an "agreement in principle" regarding Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program, but simultaneously affirmed high military readiness and demanded a "rapid deal." Secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterated that the US seeks a change in the Iranian regime's behavior and aims to raise the cost of its expansionist policies. The US State Department issued renewed warnings for its citizens in the Middle East. **Gulf States** showed divergent responses: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman urged Trump to de-escalate and expressed concern over planned US attacks, while the UAE reportedly pressed Trump for more decisive military action against Iran, including potential ground operations and taking control of Hormuz. Oman is actively mediating negotiations with Iran over a "new mechanism" for the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwaiti state-affiliated channels posted messages recalling past US defense commitments amidst Iranian threats, and a US C-17 was observed heading to Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. In **Europe**, the foreign ministries of the UK, Bulgaria, and Ukraine reportedly contacted Iran to state they would not be part of any war against it. Egypt's Foreign Minister also emphasized the necessity of de-escalation in a call with US envoy Steve Witkoff. **Russia** reported an explosion at a Moscow restaurant resulting in 3 deaths and 17 injuries, identified as an IED detonation. **Pakistan's** Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir discussed potential US attacks with Iran's FM Araghchi. **Iraq** agreed to open a NATO office in Baghdad, while its National Security Advisor and France's chargé d'affaires emphasized a return to diplomatic channels for de-escalation. OPEC+ nations, including Saudi Arabia, Russia, and Iraq, agreed to increase oil production by 188,000 barrels per day for September.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the status of the Strait of Hormuz: President Trump proclaimed an "agreement in principle" for its "immediate, complete, and total opening," while Iran's Foreign Ministry and state news agency Fars vehemently denied any such agreement, maintaining the Strait remains closed and requires IRGC Navy permission for passage. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi, while confirming negotiations with Oman on a "new mechanism," stated this does not imply reopening the Strait. Oman is reportedly seeking formal confirmation from the IRGC regarding the agreement.

The incident in Kafra, South Lebanon, also presents contradictory narratives: The Lebanese Armed Forces initially claimed an Israeli strike injured five soldiers, then recanted, stating the cause was a "suspicious object." The IDF explicitly denied any strike, asserting the explosion was caused by a Hezbollah-planted device.

Unverified claims include a report by NAYA of an LNG tanker, GasLog Shanghai, being struck by a projectile and losing power while exiting the Strait of Hormuz. This claim, if true, would significantly impact the regional assessment but lacks corroboration from other sources in the feed. Additionally, NAYA relayed a speculative claim from "observers" about Iraq being asked to open a land corridor for Iranian forces through Kuwait, contingent on various territorial and economic concessions, which appears to be propaganda. Reports of widespread internet outages in several Iranian cities (Abadan, Tabriz, Damavand, Isfahan) also remain unverified in terms of their cause and extent. Sensationalist claims, such as Channel 13 Israel's report (via Kianmeli1) that "99% of IRGC leaders have been killed," are likely propaganda and lack credibility.

Propaganda indicators are evident across multiple sources. Iranian state media and officials emphasize Iranian resilience, diplomatic maturity, and the necessity of retaliation against aggressors, while consistently denying US claims about Hormuz. Israeli media often highlight successful counter-terrorism operations and portray terror groups as the primary threat, alongside expressing frustration at US strategic ambiguity. Social media accounts like @omid_dana explicitly promote anti-regime and anti-Shia sentiments, actively call for regime change, and interpret events through a highly biased lens, often using inflammatory language, indicating a clear activist agenda rather than objective reporting. Kuwaiti government-aligned accounts engaging in nostalgic appeals for US protection against Iranian threats also serve a propaganda function.

Reporting gaps include insufficient detail on the "agreement in principle" Trump referenced, making it impossible to ascertain its veracity or scope. There is also limited independent verification of the full impact of US military deployments on civilian airport operations in Israel or the specific nature and extent of new settler attacks in the West Bank.
